1→# Changelog
     2→
     3→All notable changes to the Exhibition VM Controller project will be documented in this file.
     4→
     5→The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
     6→and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
     7→
     8→## [Unreleased]
     9→
    10→### Planned
    11→- Support for Mac OS 9 guest monitoring scripts (AppleScript-based)
    12→- Support for Linux guest monitoring scripts (shell script-based)
    13→- WebSocket API for real-time status updates
    14→- Centralized logging dashboard for multiple exhibition hosts
    15→- Automated testing framework
    16→- Docker containerization for host controller
    17→- VMware and VirtualBox backend support
    18→- Metrics collection and visualization (Prometheus/Grafana integration)
    19→- Modular plugin system for custom polling and signaling handlers
    20→
    21→## [1.3.0] - 2025-12-13
    22→
    23→### Added
    24→- **Web UI for remote VM management** - Simple, responsive web interface at `/ui/` for maintenance personnel to control VMs without SSH access
    25→  - System status dashboard showing VM state, snapshot, heartbeat activity, and auto-revert status
    26→  - VM control buttons (Start, Stop)
    27→  - Snapshot management (Create, Revert to Snapshot)
    28→  - Auto-revert toggle (Enable/Disable for maintenance mode)
    29→  - Real-time monitoring with auto-refresh every 5 seconds
    30→  - Clean single-page interface with no authentication (for trusted local networks)
    31→- **Manual stop tracking** - System distinguishes between intentional VM stop via API/UI (stays stopped) vs. guest shutdown or crash (auto-restarts)
    32→- **Improved heartbeat status tracking** - Distinguishes between actual guest heartbeats and internal monitoring timer
    33→  - Shows "Waiting" status when no heartbeat received yet
    34→  - Shows "Healthy" only when actual heartbeat received from guest
    35→  - Detailed heartbeat activity card with time since last heartbeat and health status
    36→
    37→### Changed
    38→- **Simplified heartbeat monitoring** - Monitoring is now controlled solely by `auto_revert_enabled` setting, removing redundant toggle
    39→  - Heartbeat monitoring automatically starts/stops with auto-revert enable/disable
    40→  - No more separate enable/disable of heartbeat monitoring
    41→- **Heartbeat timer initialization** - Timer now starts automatically when monitoring begins, enabling timeout detection even before first heartbeat
    42→- **VM state monitoring respects manual stops** - Auto-restart only triggers on unexpected shutdowns, not manual stops via API/UI
    43→
    44→### Fixed
    45→- Heartbeat status now correctly reports whether actual heartbeat was received from guest
    46→- Manual VM stop via API/UI no longer triggers immediate auto-restart
    47→- Web UI correctly displays heartbeat status using proper API property names
    48→
    49→### Benefits
    50→- Maintenance personnel can control VMs remotely via browser without SSH
    51→- Clear distinction between maintenance mode (manual stop) and failure recovery (auto-restart)
    52→- Accurate heartbeat status prevents false "healthy" reports when no heartbeat received
    53→- Simplified monitoring architecture easier to understand and maintain
    54→
    55→## [1.2.0] - 2025-12-13
    56→
    57→### Added
    58→- **GET request support for all API endpoints** - All POST endpoints now also accept GET requests for compatibility with AutoIt and other tools that cannot make POST requests
    59→- GET support for: `/api/v1/heartbeat`, `/api/v1/vm/start`, `/api/v1/vm/stop`, `/api/v1/vm/restart`, `/api/v1/snapshot/create`, `/api/v1/snapshot/delete/{name}`, `/api/v1/revert/enable`, `/api/v1/revert/disable`
    60→
    61→### Changed
    62→- **AutoIt compatibility** - All control endpoints can now be called with simple GET requests from AutoIt guest scripts
    63→- DELETE endpoint `/api/v1/snapshot/{name}` now also available as GET at `/api/v1/snapshot/delete/{name}`
    64→
    65→### Benefits
    66→- Enables simple HTTP control from legacy environments (Windows XP, older AutoIt versions)
    67→- No JSON parsing required for basic operations
    68→- Maintains backward compatibility with existing POST-based clients
    69→
    70→## [1.1.0] - 2025-12-13
    71→
    72→### Added
    73→- **Automatic VM startup on controller launch** - VM now automatically starts and reverts to "ready" snapshot when controller starts, ensuring clean initial state every time (commit 1551d56)
    74→- **VM state monitoring and auto-recovery** - System continuously monitors VM state (every 0.5s) and automatically restarts if VM is manually shut down or crashes (commit 1551d56)
    75→- Poetry script shortcuts (`vm-controller`, `vmctl`) for easier execution (commit 91e7871)
    76→- Link to virtio-win drivers for Windows guest setup in documentation (commit 91e7871)
    77→
    78→### Changed
    79→- **QEMU guest agent is now optional** - System works perfectly without guest agent installed; set `check_qemu_agent: false` in config (commit 91e7871)
    80→- Improved configuration documentation with clearer guidance on QEMU guest agent usage (commit 91e7871)
    81→- HeartbeatMonitor now accepts `vm_manager` parameter for VM state monitoring (commit 1551d56)
    82→
    83→### Fixed
    84→- Fixed 5-minute timeout when QEMU agent checking is disabled - now skips wait entirely, reducing revert time from 300s to 4s (commit 91e7871)
    85→- Fixed race condition in heartbeat monitoring enable/disable cycle after timeout callback (commit 91e7871)
    86→- VM restart now properly skips QEMU agent wait when `check_qemu_agent: false` (commit 91e7871)
    87→
    88→### Performance
    89→- VM revert time reduced from 300s to 4s when QEMU agent is disabled
    90→- Manual VM shutdown detection: 0.5 seconds
    91→- Auto-recovery from shutdown: ~4 seconds
    92→- Auto-revert cycle: ~29 seconds (15s timeout + 4s revert + 10s delay)
    93→
    94→## [1.0.0] - 2025-12-09
    95→
    96→### Added
    97→- Initial public release of Exhibition VM Controller
    98→- Core host controller with FastAPI REST API
    99→- VM lifecycle management via libvirt/virsh
   100→- Snapshot-based automatic recovery system
   101→- Heartbeat monitoring with configurable timeouts
   102→- QEMU guest agent integration for low-level health checks
   103→- Windows XP guest monitoring scripts (AutoIt)
   104→  - heartbeat.au3 - Periodic alive signal
   105→  - idle-monitor.au3 - User inactivity detection
   106→  - process-watchdog.au3 - Application monitoring
   107→  - run.au3 - Process launcher
   108→- Comprehensive documentation
   109→  - Architecture overview
   110→  - Getting Started guide
   111→  - Heartbeat Protocol specification
   112→  - API Reference
   113→  - Troubleshooting guide
   114→- Deployment configurations
   115→  - Systemd service templates
   116→  - Openbox autostart configuration
   117→  - Nginx reverse proxy examples
   118→- Academic publication support files
   119→  - CITATION.cff for software citation
   120→  - codemeta.json for software metadata
   121→  - .zenodo.json for DOI registration
   122→  - AUTHORS file with contributor information
   123→  - CONTRIBUTING.md with contribution guidelines
   124→- Configuration management via YAML
   125→- Python Poetry-based dependency management
   126→- MIT License
   127→
   128→### Tested
   129→- 6+ months of continuous operation in exhibition environment
   130→- "Choose Your Filter! Browser Art since the Beginnings of the World Wide Web" exhibition at ZKM Karlsruhe (February-August 2025)
   131→- 12 concurrent VM instances across multiple physical hosts
   132→- Windows XP guests with various browser-based artworks
   133→- Successful restoration of 8 historical digital artworks:
   134→  - Eden.Garden (2001) by Entropy8Zuper!
   135→  - Subfusion (2001-2002) by Stanza
   136→  - Wrong Browser Series (2001-2012) by JODI
   137→  - Browser Gestures (2001) by Mark Daggett
   138→  - ZNC browser 2.0 (2003) by Peter Luining
   139→  - <earshot> (1999) by Andy Freeman and Jason Skeets
   140→  - Reconnoitre (1997-2002) by Gavin Baily and Tom Corby
   141→
   142→### Performance
   143→- Snapshot revert: 2-5 seconds
   144→- Heartbeat interval: 1 second
   145→- Heartbeat timeout: 10 seconds (configurable)
   146→- Idle timeout: 12 minutes (configurable)
   147→- Recovery time: <10 seconds total (timeout + revert)
   148→
   149→### Supported Platforms
   150→
   151→**Host**:
   152→- Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (primary test platform)
   153→- Debian 12 (tested)
   154→- Other Linux distributions with KVM/QEMU support (should work)
   155→
   156→**Guest**:
   157→- Windows XP SP3 (extensively tested)
   158→- Windows 7 (tested)
   159→- Windows 10 (tested)
   160→- Mac OS 9 (partial support, scripts in development)
   161→- Linux guests (partial support, scripts in development)
   162→
   163→## Release Notes
   164→
   165→### Version 1.0.0 - Initial Release
   166→
   167→This is the first public release of the Exhibition VM Controller, developed at ZKM | Center for Art and Media Karlsruhe for the conservation and exhibition of historical digital artworks.
   168→
   169→**Key Features**:
   170→- **Autonomous Operation**: Runs unattended for months with automatic error recovery
   171→- **Snapshot-Based Recovery**: Deterministic restoration to known-good states
   172→- **Modular Architecture**: Clear separation between host orchestration and guest monitoring
   173→- **Exhibition-Tested**: Proven in 6+ months of real-world museum deployment
   174→- **Well Documented**: Comprehensive guides for setup, operation, and troubleshooting
   175→- **Open Source**: MIT licensed, ready for reuse by other institutions
   176→
   177→**Use Cases**:
   178→- Digital art conservation and exhibition
   179→- Historical software preservation
   180→- Legacy system emulation
   181→- Interactive museum installations
   182→- Long-term exhibition operation with minimal maintenance
   183→
   184→**Academic Context**:
   185→This software is the practical implementation of research conducted for the exhibition "Choose Your Filter! Browser Art since the Beginnings of the World Wide Web" at ZKM Karlsruhe. It demonstrates that virtualization combined with automated monitoring and snapshot-based recovery provides a robust foundation for exhibiting fragile, internet-dependent digital artworks.
   186→
   187→**Acknowledgments**:
   188→This software was created within the framework of the exhibition "Choose Your Filter! Browser Art since the Beginnings of the World Wide Web" at ZKM | Center for Art and Media Karlsruhe in cooperation with the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT).
   189→
   190→**Funding**: The German Research Foundation (DFG) and the European Research Council (ERC, under the European Union's Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement COSE, No. 101045376) funded the research projects underlying the exhibition.
   191→
   192→**Developed by**: Marc Schütze at ZKM | Center for Art and Media Karlsruhe in collaboration with Daniel Heiss, Matthieu Vlaminck, and Leonie Rök. Technical project management by Matthias Gommel.
   193→
   194→**Curated by**: Laura C. Schmidt, Inge Hinterwaldner, and Daniela Hönigsberg.
   195→
   196→Special thanks to ZKM for the opportunity to conduct this research and develop the methods described here, and to Rhizome for pioneering work in digital art preservation and emulation-based conservation.
   197→
   198→---
   199→
   200→## Version History
   201→
   202→### Pre-Release Development
   203→
   204→**2024-07 to 2025-01**: Development and testing phase
   205→- Architecture design and implementation
   206→- Testing with multiple artworks in parallel
   207→- Refinement based on exhibition operation feedback
   208→- Documentation writing
   209→
   210→**2024-02**: Project inception
   211→- Initial concept and requirements gathering
   212→- Selection of virtualization approach
   213→- First prototypes with Windows XP VMs
   214→
   215→---
   216→
   217→## Migration Guide
   218→
   219→### From Pre-Release Versions
   220→
   221→If you were using development versions of this software:
   222→
   223→1. **Configuration Changes**:
   224→   - Configuration is now YAML-based (`config.yaml`) instead of environment variables
   225→   - Copy `examples/config.example.yaml` and adapt to your setup
   226→   - Old `.env` files are no longer supported
   227→
   228→2. **API Changes**:
   229→   - API structure is stable and follows REST conventions
   230→   - Endpoints are now versioned under `/api/v1/`
   231→   - Previous development endpoints may have changed
   232→
   233→3. **Dependencies**:
   234→   - Now managed via Poetry
   235→   - Run `poetry install` to set up dependencies
   236→   - Python 3.10+ is required
   237→
   238→4. **Guest Scripts**:
   239→   - Scripts are now located in `guest-scripts/windows-xp/`
   240→   - Update host URL in scripts to match your configuration
   241→   - Recompile AutoIt scripts if using old versions
   242→

   245→## Reporting Issues

Author: marc <marc@schuetze.io>
Date:   Sat Dec 13 23:14:04 2025 +0100

    Release v1.3.0: Add web UI and simplify monitoring
    
    This release adds a web-based control panel for remote VM management
    and simplifies the heartbeat monitoring architecture.
    
    Major Features:
    - Web UI at /ui/ for browser-based VM control
    - Manual stop tracking (API stop vs guest shutdown)
    - Improved heartbeat status (actual vs timer)
    - Simplified monitoring tied to auto_revert_enabled
    
    Web UI:
    - System status dashboard
    - VM control (Start/Stop)
    - Snapshot management
    - Auto-revert toggle
    - Real-time monitoring (5s refresh)
    - No authentication (trusted networks)
    
    Monitoring Improvements:
    - Heartbeat monitoring controlled by auto_revert_enabled only
    - Timer initializes automatically when monitoring starts
    - Distinguishes actual guest heartbeats from system timer
    - Shows "Waiting" when no heartbeat, "Healthy" when received
    
    Manual Stop Handling:
    - Stop via API/UI: VM stays stopped (maintenance mode)
    - Guest shutdown: VM auto-restarts (recovery mode)
    - Heartbeat timeout: VM auto-restarts
    - Start VM: Re-enables auto-restart
    
    Version Bump: 1.2.0 → 1.3.0
    
    Files Changed:
    - static/index.html (new): Web UI implementation
    - vm_controller/api.py: Version bump, manual stop handling
    - vm_controller/heartbeat_monitor.py: Simplified monitoring, timer init
    - vm_controller/vm_manager.py: No changes needed
    - pyproject.toml: Version 1.3.0
    - README.md: Web UI documentation
    - CHANGELOG.md: Full 1.3.0 release notes

commit 956404bf8ce44f07d89ae2559701e1deb7ae58ab
Author: marc <marc@schuetze.io>
Date:   Sat Dec 13 21:49:16 2025 +0100

    Release v1.2.0 - GET Request Support for AutoIt Compatibility
    
    Add GET request support to all API endpoints for compatibility with AutoIt and other tools that cannot make POST requests.
    
    NEW FEATURES:
    - All POST endpoints now accept GET requests
    - Enables simple HTTP control from legacy environments
    - DELETE endpoint also available as GET
    
    ENDPOINTS UPDATED:
    - GET /api/v1/heartbeat
    - GET /api/v1/vm/start, stop, restart
    - GET /api/v1/snapshot/create
    - GET /api/v1/snapshot/delete/{name}
    - GET /api/v1/revert/enable, disable
    
    BENEFITS:
    - AutoIt guest scripts can control VM without POST
